title: Reversing Preferential Attachment and the Residue of the Configuration Model
content: We study a process that runs the growth step of preferential attachment backwards. A vertex may be removed only if it could have been the most recent arrival in a growth process in which every new vertex brings m edges, and removal continues until no such vertex is left. Graphs grown from a clique by attaching each new vertex to m distinct earlier vertices, which include the Barabási–Albert graphs, are always reduced to a copy of that clique. For configuration multigraphs whose empirical degree distributions and mean degrees converge to those of the same limiting law, by contrast, a positive fraction of the vertices remains, and we identify this fraction through an explicit system of differential equations. For the Barabási–Albert degree distribution, under a non-degeneracy condition that we verify numerically, the fraction lies between 0.65 and 0.86 for m = 2, . . . , 6, in agreement with simulations.
